S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder defined by persistent disturbances such as delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech or behavior, and negative symptoms, with clear social or occupational decline and a course lasting at least six months. It is distinguished from brief psychotic disorder, delusional disorder, mood disorders with psychotic features, and substance- or medical-condition-related psychosis by its duration, breadth of symptoms, functional impairment, and absence of a primary mood or toxic cause.

patient.stressor: Luis injured his shoulder and ribs during a difficult ambulance transfer, forcing him off field duty and into a light-duty desk assignment that disrupted the disciplined rhythm of runs, lifting, fishing, and night shifts. Across the following 8 months, he developed fixed beliefs tied to the injury review process, began acting in ways that alarmed coworkers during routine station operations, and gradually lost interest in cooking, playing tres, training, and meeting friends for basketball. His performance deteriorated to the point that he was removed from the schedule, and his usually reliable bilingual triage notes and equipment checks became unusable for team workflow. He entered psychiatric care through an occupational-health mandate after a station incident led supervisors to send him for emergency evaluation.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I know the injury review people and some supervisors have been watching me through the station cameras and changing my triage notes to make me look unsafe, even when they tell me it's just routine paperwork.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: They sent me here because at the station I kept moving the airway bags into a pattern I knew was right, repeating the dispatch numbers out loud, and I wouldn't step away when my lieutenant told me to stop because it felt like the whole bay would go bad if I broke the sequence.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: Most days I just sit in my apartment with the tres in the corner and food still in the fridge, not calling the guys for basketball or cooking like I used to, because I can't get myself to care or start anything.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I can’t work the ambulance anymore, and even the desk-duty notes and equipment checks got so unreliable that they took me off the schedule. I’ve also mostly stopped seeing friends or keeping up with things at home the way I used to.
add_requirements.duration: This all started after I hurt my shoulder and ribs during that ambulance transfer about eight months ago.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: The camera and paperwork stuff, and the station behavior that got everyone alarmed, have been going on for about the last two months.
